headers: access-control-allow-headers: Allow, Content-Encoding, Content-Length, Content-Type, ETag, Expires, Last-Modified, Location, Server, Vary, Authorization
access-control-allow-methods: CONNECT, DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST, PUT, PATCH, TRACE
access-control-expose-headers: Allow, Content-Encoding, Content-Length, Content-Type, ETag, Expires, Last-Modified, Location, Server, Vary, Authorization
results.note: register: an internal-$ref schema (unaffected by the SSRF gate) and a remote-$ref schema (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, guaranteed non-routable — the point is that it is never actually contacted)
shouldMatchSchemaUsingOnlyInternalRefsAsBefore: a schema with only internal ($ref: #/...) refs validates exactly as before the SSRF gate

headers: x-mockserver-closest-match-hint: expectation <uuid>: body did not match (  json schema match failed expected:     {       "type" : "object",       "definitions" : {         "positiveInt" : {           "type" : "integer",           "minimum" : 1         }  ...
results.note: shouldRejectNonMatchingBodyAgainstInternalRefSchemaAsBefore: a body violating the internal ref's minimum:1 is reported as a non-match, mentioning "count" — the gate changes nothing about internal-ref validation

headers: x-mockserver-closest-match-hint: expectation <uuid>: path did not match (  string or regex match failed expected:     /internal-ref    found:     /remote-ref )
results.note: shouldBlockRemoteRefByDefaultWithoutNetworkFetch: the remote $ref is never fetched (default deny, no opt-in) — the response comes back promptly (this step would hang/timeout if the server actually tried to reach 192.0.2.1) and the closest-match hint names the blocked reference instead of a connection failure
